p6_b2.ocr: In Table 1, the qualitative variables show that among 61 seizure-free patients, 37 experienced seizure onset to surgery within ≤1 year, while 17 of the 29 unfavorable patients had the same timing (P-value 0.854). In terms of seizure frequency, 37 seizure-free patients had rare occurrences, compared to 8 unfavorable patients, with a significant P-value of 0.034. Regarding the site of surgery, 34 seizure-free patients underwent left-side surgery, while 17 unfavorable patients did, resulting in a P-value of 0.796. The gender distribution revealed that 31 seizure-free patients were male versus 16 unfavorable males, with a P-value of 0.699. Lastly, 55 seizure-free patients received chemoradiotherapy compared to 24 unfavorable patients, yielding a P-value of 0.319.
